description: In a city known for its sleek efficiency, what happens when 180 strangers come together to build something wildly impractical: a shared library, nestled in the heartlands, fueled by love for books and belief in community? Photographer Rebecca Toh shares the quietly radical story behind Singapore’s community-funded library, where every bookshelf is a universe reflecting its owner—from a 5-year-old to a retiree. This library offers a space where time is intentionally slowed, and where there is power in collective imagination and joy of building something meaningful together. Rebecca Toh is a photographer and the visionary behind Casual Poet Library, a community-funded library nestled in the heartlands of Singapore. This unique space, built on the spirit of collaboration, allows each of its shelves to be rented and maintained by community members and a team of volunteer librarians. title: What if you could rent out your own library shelf? | Rebecca Toh | TEDxSingapore

description:
As artificial intelligence reshapes the global economy, smaller countries face a rare window of opportunity to gain strategic advantage.
In this talk, Mkhitar Hayrapetyan explores how Armenia can position itself in the emerging AI-driven world by focusing on three critical pillars: energy, high-performance computing, and human capital.
He argues that success in the AI era will depend not on size, but on clarity of strategy, consistency of execution, and the ability to align these key resources toward a shared national vision. Mkhitar Hayrapetyan is the Minister of High-Tech Industry of the Republic of Armenia, with a career spanning public policy, technology, and civic engagement.
He previously served as Minister of Diaspora and as a Member of the National Assembly, where he chaired the Standing Committee on Science, Education, Culture, Diaspora, Youth, and Sport.

Like many peers, I tried packaging my interests into an impressive resume searching for the 'perfect' path. I realized that rather than chasing the 'optimal' passion, it's more important to stay true to choices that genuinely move us—because what resonates with others is genuine enthusiasm that lights up our eyes. Passion isn't a tool to decorate resumes, but the power that shapes us. Whether documenting campus life through a camera lens or bringing whimsical designs to life with a sewing machine, I seek moments that make me feel alive. description:
"Work hard" and "don't be lazy" are often emphasized, but real major breakthroughs often come from "strategic laziness." The brain has two modes: focused mode and diffuse mode. The diffuse mode (such as during rest or relaxation) activates the default mode network, which boosts creativity and insight. The lizard brain, on the other hand, makes people fear risk and cling to busyness. Therefore, resting properly and allowing the mind to wander is not a waste of time, but the key to sparking creativity. Laziness should be seen as a partner to creativity.
 I'm a person who loves to explore and ask "why." I'm never really satisfied with just a simple answer to a question. I enjoy digging deeper, turning things over in my mind, and trying to figure out how they really work. You could say I'm a naturally curious and independent thinker. I use two main tools on my adventures. The first is math. To me, math is like a super powerful flashlight. It helps me see the clear patterns and logical ste
title: The Other Side of Laziness: Hotbed for Creativity | Chen Skyler | TEDxNACIS Shanghai Youth

author: TEDx Talks
description:
"The theme of my speech is "The Architecture of the Box: Redesigning Our Mental Framework". In my journey toward climate solutions, I’ve realized that while life presents us with a "box of chocolates," we must look beyond the problems themselves and examine the "box"—our underlying mental frameworks. My core message is that the most powerful catalyst for change is not technology alone, but the systems we build and the transformation of our thinking.
Drawing from my experiences at Oxford, Belgium, and MIT, I illustrate how my perspective shifted from isolated innovations to interconnected global systems. I hope to inspire the audience to audit their own ""mental infrastructure"". I want them to ask whether they are brave enough to let go of limiting certainties and allow new ideas to fundamentally redesign who they are. Ultimately, we must not just "Think Again," but "Build Again"" I am Yolanda Zhu, a founding student at NACIS since 2017 and a trailblazer who believes life is either a

author: TEDx Talks
description: This talk explores the power of rethinking and advocates thoughtful, open hesitation over blind certainty. We are often trapped by certainty and confirmation bias, we wired our beliefs with our identity, yet the world is ever-changing and yesterday’s truth may not hold today. The core idea is: by asking “What if I’m wrong?”, separating conviction from self, understanding opposing views, and embracing cognitive updates, we keep growing. Real progress lies not in being right at once, but in getting it right over a lifetime. Greetings! I'm Kevin, in Grade 8. For most of my school days, I've been given maps — in textbooks, lessons and advice about 'how things are done.' But I've always wondered… what if the map is wrong? We're told to follow paths others have chosen: get grades, fit into the system. But does success only depend on navigating others' maps? What if the real skill is learning to draw our own? I started questioning why things are set up as they are — in group projects, discus

description: This speech explores how seasons influence our emotions. It reveals the factors from biological and psychological perspectives, and offers three practical suggestions for campus life: steal the light, stay social and swap the scenery. It calls on us to meet our shifting emotions with curiosity instead of judgment. May everyone learn to pause, reflect on their feelings and think again! If I encounter a field, barren or fertile; a body of water, dried up or vast; a forest, mysterious or perilous, I embrace each with passion to explore—for traces of life can be found everywhere. Biological evolution's magnificent spectacle is the phenomenon, while life's unceasing cycle instinct is the essence. Civilization's inheritance and development threads are the phenomenon, while humanity's wisdom for coexisting with nature is the essence. It points out that science is everywhere in life and serves as a tool to understand and handle daily trivial matters. The core view is: science should not only be textbook knowledge, but also a way of observing the world and a superpower owned by everyone. I'm a curious thinker who uncovers the quiet superpower of science hidden in the chaos of our everyday lives. For me, science is never an esoteric concept confined to textbooks or lab benches. It's an invisible force woven into every mundane moment, the underlying logic behind life's trivial chaos and an extraordinary power lurking in our daily routines. I'm passionate about digging out these overlooked truths and revealing how science shapes our choices, empowers small actions and turns the unremarkable into something amazing. Through books, I walk in a million different shoes—an experience that has gifted me with open-mindedness, critical thought and a compassionate heart. I hold a deep conviction that with enough effort, anyone can shine as brightly as the stars. I also feel a profound duty to defend justice and peace, rejecting bullying in all its forms. description: My talk is titled “Think Again.” Using the true story of Judge Frank Caprio from a municipal courtroom in Rhode Island, I explore how we can rethink the nature of justice, success, and human connection within seemingly rigid rules and systems. I walk the line between reason and heart. Logic guides my understanding, while feeling connects me to life. I find poetry in delicate kindness, and power in thoughts that can reshape reality. I observe, but I think deeper. I look for the person behind the rule, the story behind what’s seen, and the quiet ties that bind us. This led me to the truth: we each hold an invisible gavel. It can divide or connect. The choice is ours: to judge quickly, or to listen first. To condemn, or to comprehend. That’s why I’m here—to speak about this gavel we carry. When we turn it from a tool for judgment into a tool for understanding, we don’t just decide a moment. We begin to build a kinder world. I’m Vivi. I believe thought can be gentle, can be warm, and can
title: Think Again: The Gavel of Grace | Wang Vivi | TEDxNACIS Shanghai Youth

author: TEDx Talks
description:
Where is the line between friendship and bullying—and why is it so often blurred?

This talk examines how harmful behavior can be disguised as humor, loyalty, or “just joking,” making it difficult to recognize when a friendship turns toxic. It explores the subtle forms of bullying that occur within social circles, where trust is expected but not always honored.

Through real-life dynamics and honest reflection, the talk highlights the emotional impact of exclusion, pressure, and repeated negative interactions. It also addresses why people tolerate such behavior—and how silence can reinforce it.

Ultimately, this talk challenges the audience to rethink what true friendship looks like, set clearer boundaries, and recognize that respect—not fear or conformity—is the foundation of any meaningful relationship. Jimi Nomingerel is an actress at FAVWAY production who focuses on portraying social and psychological issues affecting young people through her performances. She aims to raise awaren
title: Bullying and Friendship | Nomingerel Jimi | TEDxECL

A lo largo de la charla, propone una ruta práctica y humana para recuperar el equilibrio emocional, reconectar con el presente y construir una vida guiada por el bienestar y el propósito.

description:
Una de las características universales del cáncer es su aparente inmortalidad celular. A diferencia de las células sanas, que tienen un número limitado de divisiones, las células cancerosas logran evadir este límite y multiplicarse indefinidamente. En esta charla exploraremos qué mecanismos les otorgan esa “inmortalidad” y, sobre todo, cómo la ciencia busca arrebatársela para convertirla en su mayor debilidad. María Blasco es una líder mundial en biología de telómeros. Ha transformado la comprensión del envejecimiento, el cáncer y la regeneración tisular, generando modelos, herramientas y terapias pioneras que sitúan a los telómeros como eje terapéutico y biomédico global.

En 1997 inició su propio grupo en el Centro Nacional de Biotecnología y en 2003 se incorporó al  CNIO como Directora del Programa de Oncología Molecular y jefa del Grupo de Telómeros y Telomerasa.

Ha sido Subdirectora (2005–2011) y Directora del CNIO (2011–2025).

Es autora de 302 publicaciones, 38 en revistas de
title: Robar la Inmortalidad al Cáncer | María Blasco | TEDxUC3M
